content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have some [product_name] devices with [article_no] at home. I tried to use network input from one device to another, but if I press a push button for a very short time on the slave device, the signal is not recognized by the master. I have to use an off delay timer of 0.5s to make sure the signal reaches the master and employ a V table exchange. My question is: Is the handling of network inputs the same in devices with [article_no], and have you noticed any lag when using this feature? I have a project for a villa needing 12 devices, so this is quite important for me. Best regards, [user_name]

A delay is present with the [product_name] series using [article_no] as well. The exact time depends heavily on both the network and cycle time. I cannot specify the precise timing. In tests with two [product_name] units and a minimal program, 0.05s was unreliable—sometimes it worked, sometimes it didn't. Reliable transmission started only from 0.1s. To reiterate, that was just two units and a basic program.
A new question posted by [user_name] has been split into a separate thread titled 'Multiple devices, can I use the maximum network inputs/outputs in each device?'. Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience lag when transferring network input signals between [product_name] modules using [article_no], resulting in missed short-duration signals unless an artificial delay is introduced. This affects real-time detection and reliability, especially with many interconnected units. The delay varies depending on the network and device cycle times, and signals shorter than 0.1s are not reliably transmitted.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want fast and dependable network input signal transfer for short digital signals between multiple [product_name] modules, ideally without needing to add artificial delays.
